headline: P0155 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share of 15.2% vs 4.3% expected for its patient mix, with the excess concentrated in moderate-complexity (2-3 condition) visits
rationale: P0155 billed 47 of 310 claims (15.2%) as 99215. The expected share for this patient panel's complexity is 4.3% (risk-adjusted score 3.48), although the raw peer z-score is only modest (1.48). The panel does not explain the gap. The provider's 99215 share is above the all-provider rate in every complexity stratum. The largest excess is in moderate-complexity visits: 18.4% vs 5.6% at 2 conditions and 18.6% vs 8.7% at 3 conditions. Those strata account for 25 of the 47 99215s. On low-complexity patients the absolute numbers are small: 6 of 123 visits (5.0% vs 2.1% and 4.8% vs 3.4%). Even so, the sampled examples include single-problem diagnoses billed at the highest level: low back pain with no chronic conditions (C0071404), a UTI with no chronic conditions (C0071411), and obesity with a follow-up code (C0071599). In contrast, heart failure (C0071579) could plausibly support high complexity. The 99215s on patients with 4 or more conditions, such as C0071515 and C0071428 (elderly, multimorbid), look clinically plausible. The 5+ stratum also exceeds peers (58.3% vs 29.8%), but it has only 12 visits. Overall, the pattern is consistent with systematic upward coding rather than a uniquely sick panel. However, the claim lists are random samples, and no clinical documentation, MDM details or visit times are available to confirm whether any individual level is supported.
next_steps: Request medical records for the sampled low-complexity 99215s (C0071404, C0071411, C0071599, C0071579). Check the MDM elements (problems, data reviewed, risk) or the documented total time against 2021+ E/M criteria.
Pull a documentation sample of 99215s on 2-3 condition patients, where most of the excess sits; that stratum has not been sampled at the claim level in this packet.
Check whether 99215s cluster by date, place of service or diagnosis (e.g. R10.9, Z09 follow-ups), and whether visit-time attestations are templated or repeated.
Compare the 99214 share (154 of 310) with peers to see whether upward shift also affects the 99213/99214 boundary.
Verify the complexity attribution (chronic condition counts) against the full claims history so that under-captured comorbidities are not mistaken for upcoding.
